## Summary

Pre-release review of the driver before 4.2, probing rather than reading: five hypotheses became throwaway tests, four confirmed with numbers. Two outright bugs, fixed. A thrown Error with a blank message made the run_stopped payload invalid, so the append was refused, drive threw, and the log kept a run_started nothing closed — the exact outcome the catch around the loop exists to prevent, reached through the catch itself; errorNote now guarantees a non-empty note. And every ClaudeCodeSession leaked its temp dir: 515 sat in TMPDIR, 83 still holding a run permission surface. The dir is now removed when the exit settles, verified at zero new dirs across a full suite plus two smoke runs. Two more measured and, on the operator call, stated rather than fixed: cost cap and max sessions are per-DRIVER, and across one resume a 6 dollar cap spent 20 and a 4-session budget launched 8, because what an earlier driver spent is not an event and an unresolved launch files no handoff. Two opening warnings say so and SPEC names the limit. Then the two gaps the operator chose to close. Hang guard: a wedged agent could hang an unattended run forever, since the operator interrupt sent one SIGTERM and the driver own handler swallowed every one after. awaitSession now bounds one launch through a stated timeout, escalates SIGTERM to SIGKILL, and finally synthesises an exit; a second interrupt escalates rather than killing the driver, so the run still gets its stop. Verified live: a 60-second sleeping agent died at 2.07s. Flag vocabulary: auto and manual are real Claude Code 2.1.251 modes sofar refused, and since the driver builds the child argv, a mode sofar refuses is one no operator can reach; both added, mapped in codex, and the codex test rewritten to read from PERMISSION_MODES instead of proving the codex map maps itself. The escape hatch meant to absorb that gap had no door, so agent-arg is wired and appends last. 12 new tests, 1863 passing, typecheck clean, diff in 11 files. Three decisions and one repo memory logged.</summary>
